findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed employees donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was abolished. Ensure that employees practice adequate handwashing before donning gloves at all times.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspector was unable to verify food handler training certification during today’s inspection. PIC said that those documents were locked away and they had no access to them. Inspector told PIC to have copies of certifications in a folder accessible for inspection purposes. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.comment:
Observed the steam table was not hot holding foods at 135F or above. The water in the steam table had an ambient air temperature of 136F which an employee stated was much lower than usual. The gravy had an internal temperature of 120F and a brown sauce had an internal temperature of 107F. Other foods in the steam table included a casserole and various other sauces. The PIC stated the foods were set in the steam table this morning and they go through them very quickly. All the sauces were reheated back up to 165F. The inspector created a paper with the name of the food, the time it was set in the steam table, and the time it must be discarded. When the time the food must be discarded is reached, the food cannot be saved; it must be thrown away. The facility should use time as control for the foods in the steam table until it can hot hold foods at the proper temperature. When new foods are put in the steam table the discard time must be written on the paper. The inspector suggests getting immediate service on the steam table. The inspector will return on 09/10/2024 to check on the steam table temperature.

findings.comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. Observed two large containers of cheese in walk-in refrigerator at 100 degrees. According to kitchen staff, the food had been in there for 1 hour (a staff member had placed it there before taking a break). The containers are observed sealed completely with Saran Wrap in large containers. Method of cooling is inadequate, food is not cooling quickly. Discussed with PIC Ann and kitchen staff Greg. See that staff monitor the first 2 hours of cooling in an ice bath prior to placing food items in walk-in. See that cooling items are left uncovered to facilitate the transfer of heat away from the product.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

In kitchen prep cooler observed a tray of raw meatballs temped (x2) with a probe thermometer at 53 degrees, and a pan of sliced deli ham temped (x2) with a probe thermometer at 47-49 degrees. Kitchen employee was unaware how long food had been out of temperature in prep cooler. Both trays were voluntarily discarded at time of inspection by kitchen employees.

findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf).

Whole deli ham observed in prep cooler with a date mark of 5/14, which exceeds 7-day date mark. Discussed with PIC. Ensure foods are only kept for a maximum of 7 days, with day of defrost/preparation as day 1. Deli ham was voluntarily discarded at time of inspection.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (P)

Observed two large containers of cheese in stainless steel refrigerator at 133 degrees. According to kitchen staff, the food had been in there for 1.5 hours. Method of cooling is inadequate, food is not cooling quickly. This is a repeat violation. Discussed with PIC Ann and kitchen staff. Food must be rapidly cooled from 135 to 70 in first two hours, then 70-41 in the following 4 hours, equaling a 6 hour total cooling process.

Approved cooling methods include: breaking down food into shallow containers, rapidly cooling via an ice bath, or using an ice wand or ice as an ingredient in the food item (if possible, such as soups). Multiple methods may be used simultaneously as well. 
Foods in an active cooling process also may be uncovered to allow heat to escape properly, as long as the food is stored in a way it won't be contaminated by something else. 

Corrective action: food removed from cooler and placed back on stove for a rapid reheat to 165. After heating, both containers of cheese were placed into a deep ice bath. Inspector checked temperature at 15 minute mark, food observed at 135 degrees. At the 30 minute mark, food observed at 110 degrees. At the 45 minute mark, food observed at 90 degrees. After the 1 hour mark, food was placed in the walk-in cooler to continue cooling. Conduct periodic checks of cheese to ensure proper cooling time and temperatures are met.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:

Method of cooling was inadequate. Facility utilizes ice pans to cool, but the item being cooled was in too large a quantity to cool from 135-70 in two hours.
